record.paper_title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
record.original_question: Can one develop a continuous analogue of billiards with particles of positive and negative mass, or pseudo-Euclidean billiards, and are there interesting phenomena related to Euler-type equations for a fluid with negative density?

evidence.quote: one may expect interesting phenomena related to Euler-like equations

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a discrete dynamical system of point particles in a bounded domain in Euclidean space (or more generally in a pseudo-Euclidean space with an indefinite quadratic form on the velocity space), where particles are allowed to carry either positive or negative mass. Collisions between particles are governed by conservation of momentum and kinetic energy with respect to the (possibly indefinite) mass form, generalizing the classical theory of billiards (in which a gas of equal-mass particles in a box corresponds, after symmetrization, to billiard motion in a polytope).

(a) Construct a continuum (hydrodynamic) limit of such a system of interacting particles with mixed positive and negative masses, yielding a system of Euler-type partial differential equations governing the evolution of a compressible inviscid fluid whose density field is allowed to take both positive and negative values, together with appropriate boundary conditions modeling reflections off the walls of the container.

(b) Formulate and analyze the resulting "pseudo-Euclidean billiard" dynamics: existence and uniqueness of trajectories, behavior at collisions where the effective mass vanishes, integrability versus chaos, and ergodic properties.

(c) Identify and rigorously establish qualitative phenomena (e.g., concentration, blow-up, instability, or new conservation laws) for the Euler-type equations of such a negative-density fluid that have no analogue in the classical positive-density case.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as a speculative research direction (developing a continuous/fluid analogue of billiards with mixed-sign masses and studying associated Euler-type equations). No published work appears to give a complete construction or analysis of such a hydrodynamic limit with negative density. The status is open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems in billiards and quantitative symplectic geometry
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems including the suggestion that interesting phenomena may arise from Euler-like equations for fluids with negative density.
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed as an open problem with no known resolution.
